clue.text: Declared primarily pleasant to consume?

indicators.note: the word for declared swallows up the next piece, so it holds it inside

parts.note: declared means said, stated

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of pleasant is used

explanation.surface: A question about whether something announced as nice is good to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes P from pleasant, and 'to consume' puts it inside SAID; the whole clue also describes the answer, an old word for tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid is a rare word for savoury or palatable, so food described thus is agreeable to eat.

clue.text: Maintain position it's good to pay for drinks outside

indicators.note: the drinks phrase sits outside the next piece, wrapping it

parts.note: to buy everyone a round in a pub is to stand one's round

explanation.surface: A drinker reasons that buying the round keeps one's place at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs a group takes turns buying drinks for all, a 'round'; 'outside' wraps that phrase around G.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse to retreat or yield is idiomatically to hold firm where one stands.

clue.text: Opening part of primrose, and others

definitions.text: Opening part of primrose, and others

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of primrose

parts.note: et al is the Latin abbreviation for 'and others'

explanation.surface: A botanist describes a flower part found in primroses and other plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' takes P from primrose; the whole clue also describes the answer, which opens out as a flower blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured leaflike segment of a flower's corolla unfolds as it blooms, and primroses have five.

clue.text: Vessel carried by a hundred Germans

indicators.note: the run of letters is carried inside the words that follow, hundred Germans

explanation.surface: A ship transporting a hundred German passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' signals letters inside 'hunDRED GERmans'; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a boat that scoops silt from harbour and river beds.

clue.text: Give some corn to small island bird

parts.note: chaff is the husk part of grain, so a portion of corn
an inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: Someone feeds grain to a bird living on a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' and 'to' just join the pieces; INCH, a small island, is common in Scottish place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaffinch is a common European finch with a pink breast.

clue.text: Censor is firm about a Times leader

indicators.note: the firm's letters go around the next pieces, as about means surrounding

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: a leader is the front letter, here of Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper firm reacts to its top article being censored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes T from Times; 'about' puts A and T inside CO. A leader is also a newspaper editorial, which is the surface's bait.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and is known as Cato the Censor.

clue.text: Like original art cheaply reproduced

indicators.note: reproduced suggests something made over again, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Cheap copies of an artwork made in the style of the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' rearranges ARTCHEAPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Archetypal describes a first model or prototype from which copies come.

clue.text: Sack member producing weapon

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An employee is dismissed and produces a gun in revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a weapon that fires bullets.

clue.text: Book's clear English about free love

indicators.note: the clear-and-English letters go round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: nett means clear, as profit after deductions

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: A book plainly in English about free love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' is the anagram signal on 'love', not part of a phrase 'free love'; 'about' wraps the clear-plus-English letters round the result, just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, often light and romantic, so a type of book.

clue.text: Where people learn to live together?

definitions.text: Where people learn to live together?

parts.words: Where people learn to live together?
parts.note: sounds like a course in getting along with others, but means the building where university students lodge side by side

explanation.surface: Where people learn to live together?
explanation.definitionFit: A student hostel at a university houses students who are there to study.

clue.text: Genuine article guarded by relative in charge

indicators.note: the article is guarded by the relative, so it goes inside

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A real item kept safe by a family member who is the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real, not fake.

clue.text: Composer to make things complicated — or vice versa

definitions.meaning: Maurice ... was the French composer of Bolero

definitions.text: to make things complicated — or vice versa
definitions.meaning: the verb means both to tangle and to untangle

explanation.definitionFit: Ravel is both the French composer and a verb meaning entangle or unravel.

clue.text: Flood in river trapping tug

indicators.note: the river traps the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to lug is to pull or tug

explanation.surface: A tugboat stuck in a flooded river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland; 'tug' is a verb here, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or downpour.

clue.text: Quarters Ottoman leader ordered a girl into?

definitions.text: Quarters Ottoman leader ordered a girl into?

parts.note: S and E are compass quarters, south and east

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Ottoman

explanation.surface: Asks which part of the palace a sultan commanded a girl to enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns A GIRL into RAGIL; 'leader' takes O from Ottoman. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The seraglio was the women's apartments of an Ottoman palace, a harem.

clue.text: Lethargic type of general captured by top agent

indicators.note: the general is captured by the agent, held inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
the head is the top

explanation.surface: A general is caught by a senior spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert E Lee was the American Civil War general; 'top agent' reads as a spymaster but splits into two pieces, with 'captured by' working only on 'agent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepyhead is a drowsy, sluggish person.

clue.text: Old city in part of Africa extremely lively, of course

indicators.note: the old city goes in the part of Africa

parts.note: Natal is a province of South Africa
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

indicators.note: the extremes of lively are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An ancient city in Africa that is very lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives LY from lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally, like 'of course', means as expected, obviously.

clue.text: Try changing woman's despotic rules

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters of try

parts.note: Annie's, a woman's name with the possessive

explanation.surface: A woman tries to change oppressive rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' turns TRY into TYR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannies are cruel, oppressive forms of government.

clue.text: Heard rhythmic arrangement for recorder

indicators.note: heard says the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: metre is the rhythmic pattern in verse

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a rhythmic piece arranged for the recorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' looks like the instrument but is a measuring device.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is a device measuring and recording, like a gas meter.

clue.text: Astute wife discarded fragment of cloth, possibly

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: shrewd means astute

explanation.surface: A clever wife throws out a scrap of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a strip or scrap, of cloth for example.

clue.text: Titled woman contributing regular payment to staff rise

indicators.note: the payment contributes itself into the reversed staff, going inside
in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rod is a staff
a wage is a regular payment

explanation.surface: A noblewoman gives a pay rise to her staff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' reads the staff word upwards; 'regular payment' is one phrase for earnings, not a pick of alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband.

clue.text: Insist upon Head producing nice behaviour

parts.note: to exact is to demand, insist upon
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Demanding that the headteacher produces good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' here means precise, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is precision, and 'nice' in an old sense means finely precise.

clue.text: Hysterics as dentist finally gets to cavity

indicators.note: finally points at the end letter of dentist

parts.note: an antrum is an anatomical cavity, as in the sinus

explanation.surface: A patient panics as the dentist reaches the cavity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an uncontrolled fit of rage, a burst of hysterics.

clue.text: Fugitives are found in parts of airport

indicators.note: the unit is found inside the airport parts

parts.note: runways are parts of an airport
A is the abbreviation for are, a metric unit of area

explanation.surface: Escaped criminals turn up on the airport tarmac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is the metric area unit of 100 square metres, giving A.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaways are people who have fled, fugitives.

clue.text: Heading for the front, where one's sister may be

definitions.meaning: a sister is a senior nurse in Britain, working on a hospital ward

explanation.definitionFit: Onward means forward; 'on ward' is where a hospital nurse is working.

clue.text: Description of class that includes hobbies

definitions.text: Description of class that includes hobbies

parts.words: Description of class that includes hobbies
parts.note: hobbies sounds like pastimes, but a hobby is a small falcon, so the class is the birds

explanation.surface: Description of class that includes hobbies
explanation.definitionFit: Avian means relating to birds, and the hobby is a falcon.

clue.text: Another bird, seen outside with gull or loon

indicators.note: the bird is seen outside the next letter, wrapping it

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A bird watched among gulls and loons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' and 'loon' look like birds but mean fools.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a fool; a gull is a dupe and a loon a crazy person.

clue.text: Taking advantage of university to make notes

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes

explanation.surface: A student uses the university to take notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Using someone means exploiting or taking advantage of them.

clue.text: Many of this age ordered to go to war and die

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many in that era were ordered to fight and perish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges WARANDDIE; 'to go to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardians lived in Edward VII's reign, 1901 to 1910, many dying in the Great War soon after.

clue.text: Its race did badly, without a doubt

indicators.note: badly means the letters are mixed up
without says a letter is left out of the mixed letters

explanation.surface: A horse race went poorly, no question about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' mixes ITSRACEDID and 'without' drops the A from them to leave the answer. 'did' looks like part of the surface verb but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to doubt or disbelieve it.

clue.text: Ministerial accommodation Poles established in West

indicators.note: the poles are established inside the next name

parts.note: Mae West was the American actress
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish people settle in the western part of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' is Mae West, not a direction; the house is a minister's.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is a house provided for a Presbyterian minister.
